title: the seal step records the KEK back end it used; install.sh copies it to deploy/.env
note: basis 'shown' means shown by the card's unit tests with the stand-in systemd-creds of the existing seal tests; not run on a real box or TPM.

findings.claim: after an install nothing on the box recorded which KEK back end sealed the site keys (install-test F-22); seal_keys.sh --record now writes it (install.sh: deploy/site/kek-backend) only after its last step passed, and install.sh copies it to deploy/.env TB_KEK_BACKEND without working it out itself

the box's deferred seal (TB_BOX_DEFER_SEAL=1, box-install.sh apply step) runs seal_keys.sh without --record, so nothing records the back end there, so the host check there still reads hardening.conf or tpm
